papers.title: Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.
papers.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in o
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance directly from chemical structures and uses these predictions to flag the risk of ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics at early drug-discovery stages. This offers a complementary screening tool to physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling when experimental data are limited.

papers.title: Integrative network pharmacology and experimental evaluation reveal TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia umbellata latex is used in Brazilian traditional medicine, including empirically for cancer treatment. However, its chemical composition, molecular targets, pharmacological properties, and biological effects in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of E. umbellata crude latex by integrating computational analyses with experimental evaluation in a 4T1 cell model. Eighteen compounds previously identified in E. umbellata crude latex were curated from phytochemical studies and ev
papers.summary: This study combined computational network pharmacology with experimental testing in 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer cells to characterize the anti-cancer activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex, a plant used in Brazilian traditional medicine. The authors curated 18 known latex compounds, predicted their molecular targets and pathways, and then validated key findings experimentally, identifying potential TNBC-relevant mechanisms alongside toxicity concerns.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of novel hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-based sulfonamide derivatives 9-12a-j were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE). Compounds 9a and 9b exhibited potent dual cholinesterase inhibition, with IC50 values of 9.04 and 8.61 µM against AChE and 3.08 and 4.64 µM against BChE, respectively. Compound 12j emerged as the most potent BChE inhibitor of the series (IC50 = 1.06 ± 0.11 µM), displaying pronounced BChE preference (SI = 10.37), whereas 9d showed the highest BChE selectivity (BChE IC50 = 4.18 ± 0.56 µ
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of hybrid molecules combining benzene sulfonamide and [1,4]benzoxazepine scaffolds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes targeted in Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 ~1 µM) and showing selectivity for BChE over AChE. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding. This is early-stage medicinal chemistry work with in vitro data only.

papers.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized a series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrid compounds using click chemistry and tested them as dual inhibitors of EGFR and CDK1, two kinases involved in cancer cell growth and division. The compounds showed antiproliferative activity against a panel of four human cancer cell lines, and the authors used computational (in silico) docking studies to rationalize the binding to both targets. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying a new scaffold for dual-target cancer therapy.

papers.title: A Machine Learning-Enhanced Ligand-Based Workflow Identifies Novel Cryptosporidium parvum Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Cryptosporidium parasites are a leading cause of waterborne disease worldwide, causing life-threatening diarrhea and malnutrition in young children and people with HIV. Currently, nitazoxanide is the only FDA-approved treatment, but it is largely ineffective in severely immunocompromised patients, highlighting the need for new therapies. Here, we use a ligand-based virtual screening workflow that integrates Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to screen a subset of Enamine's REAL database comprising 51 million virtual compounds. Across two screening campa
papers.summary: The authors developed a ligand-based virtual screening workflow combining Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to search 51 million virtual compounds from Enamine's REAL database for new Cryptosporidium parvum inhibitors. This approach identified novel candidate compounds against a parasite for which nitazoxanide is the only approved—and often ineffective—treatment.

papers.title: Drug Design and Discovery: The Long Road From Hansch Analysis to Artificial Intelligence.
papers.abstract: The present article traces the long journey of the historical evolution and transformation of QSAR from its early days to its current role in drug discovery. It begins with the breakthrough created by the introduction of data analysis and highlights the major advances achieved throughout its development. Changes in molecular representation resulted in an explosion of molecular descriptors, while the rapid accumulation of large amounts of data demanded the application of elaborated statistical techniques. Today, machine learning and artificial intelligence have become integral components of pha
papers.summary: This review traces the historical evolution of QSAR (quantitative structure-activity relationships) from Hansch analysis through the explosion of molecular descriptors and statistical methods to the current integration of machine learning and artificial intelligence in drug discovery. It highlights how changes in molecular representation and data accumulation have shaped computational drug design, positioning AI as a central component of modern pharmaceutical research.

papers.title: From Generative Molecular Design to Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced the early stages of drug discovery, which focus primarily on target evaluation and the design or identification of new active small molecules or biologics. Deep neural networks adapted from areas such as natural language processing and computer vision have provided novel opportunities for generative modeling and human-machine interactions. State-of-the-art AI models for generative molecular design have emerged, but remain only little understood so far. Furthermore, new computational systems are being devised rapidly
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of AI in early-stage drug discovery, from deep-learning-based generative models for designing small molecules and biologics to emerging agentic AI systems that can autonomously plan and execute tasks. It highlights that while state-of-the-art generative models exist, their behavior remains poorly understood, and rapid advances in agentic computational systems are reshaping human-machine interaction in target evaluation and molecule identification.

papers.title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides.
papers.abstract: Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI - a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed a
papers.summary: Pepti-DrugPhAI is a multimodal AI tool that predicts pharmacokinetic properties and toxicity for peptide drug candidates, addressing a major bottleneck in peptide therapeutic development. It integrates multiple data modalities to provide comprehensive ADMET predictions, aiming to reduce late-stage failures in preclinical and clinical trials.

papers.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me
papers.summary: Researchers synthesized and characterized a new organic-inorganic copper(II) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], using X-ray crystallography, DFT, molecular docking, optical spectroscopy, and biological assays. The compound features discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions held in a 3D supramolecular network by hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and halogen contacts, and shows semiconducting behavior with a ~2.5 eV band gap plus broad visible emission. The work links structure to optical and biological properties, though the abstract is truncated before biological results are described.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane compound and characterized it spectroscopically, then used DFT calculations and molecular docking to assess its potential as an inhibitor of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1, a cancer drug target. Docking suggested a modest binding affinity (-5.678 kcal/mol) that outperformed a comparator, but no experimental validation of binding or cellular activity was reported.

papers.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences.
papers.summary: GPCRAgent is a multi-agent platform that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to support GPCR-targeted drug discovery. It addresses the limitations of standalone LLMs by integrating structured GPCR domain knowledge, aiming to improve interpretability and systematic characterization of receptor functions and ligand interactions.

papers.title: QRxVision: Multimodal QR Encoding and Computer Vision for Domain-Specific Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Computational approaches applied to the drug discovery pipeline are invaluable because of their overall speed or time to solution, sustainability, accessibility combined with ever improving accuracy. Furthermore, the high-throughput virtual screening supports practical sampling of the vast chemical space for target-relevant bioactive compounds that can be experimentally validated further downstream in the drug development process. The current paradigm being practiced in computer-aided drug screening strategies centers around structure-based and ligand-based approaches supported by a range of c
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: QRxVision introduces a multimodal framework that combines QR-code-like encoding of molecular data with computer vision to enable domain-specific drug discovery. The approach aims to improve high-throughput virtual screening by representing chemical information in a format amenable to image-based deep learning, potentially increasing accuracy and accessibility. It offers a new way to integrate molecular representations with vision models for target-relevant compound identification.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic datasets to identify HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key epigenetic targets, then tests sodium propionate (SP) as an HDAC inhibitor in HCC cells. The authors report that SP shows anticancer activity in vitro, linked to downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work combines computational target identification with preliminary experimental validation.

papers.title: Strengthening Japan's drug discovery and medical research ecosystem: AMED's innovation challenge.
papers.abstract: Japan continues to face challenges in translating life science and medical research into innovative medicines and healthcare technologies. The Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED), established in 2015, plays a central role in bridging basic research and practical application. To address gaps between research and development stages and to promote practical application of promising technological seeds from academia, AMED adopted five strategic priorities under its Third Mid- to Long-Term Plan (2025-2029). (1) Strengthen coordination across AMED programs to ensure seamless sup
papers.summary: This paper describes how AMED, Japan's main medical research funding agency, is restructuring its programs to better translate basic life science research into practical medicines and healthcare technologies. It outlines five strategic priorities under AMED's 2025-2029 plan, emphasizing coordination across programs to create seamless support from discovery through application.

papers.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a suc
papers.summary: This paper describes a short undergraduate laboratory activity that teaches students how to use generative AI tools to design nanobodies against viral targets, replacing the months-long animal immunization and phage display workflow with a computational exercise. The activity makes AI-driven protein design accessible in a standard class session and introduces students to an emerging approach in antiviral biologics discovery.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: The authors synthesized seventeen thymol-based ester derivatives using cinnamoyl coupling chemistry and screened them for anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines and normal fibroblasts. One derivative, TM7, emerged as the most promising antiproliferative agent, and molecular docking was used to rationalize its binding to a likely target. The work is a standard medicinal chemistry design-synthesis-screen study with preliminary biological evaluation.

papers.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, umbrella sampling, and toxicity prediction to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential inhibitors of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), a cancer drug target. A CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies and identified 26 compounds with strong predicted affinity, which were then refined through docking and simulation-based free energy calculations. The work nominates candidate natural-product ALK inhibitors for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules combining paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking analysis supporting the design rationale.

papers.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitory evaluation of prenylated flavonoids from peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) shells: in vitro and in silico molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Sustainable agriculture has become a crucial priority because the improper management of agricultural waste currently contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, as well as soil and air pollution. The shells of Arachis hypogaea L., which is commonly discarded as an agricultural by-product, have been reported to contain various secondary metabolites, including flavonoids, stilbenes, triterpenoids, etc. This work led to the isolation of two new prenylated flavonoids, arachisflavones A (1) and B (2), together with five prenylated flavones (3-7), two prenylated chalcones (8-9), and three prenylated f
papers.summary: This study isolated two new prenylated flavonoids (arachisflavones A and B) along with several known prenylated flavones and chalcones from peanut shells, an agricultural waste product. The compounds were tested for xanthine oxidase inhibition in vitro and evaluated via molecular docking, identifying prenylated flavonoids as potential natural xanthine oxidase inhibitors. The work highlights peanut shells as a sustainable source of bioactive compounds with possible relevance to gout or hyperuricemia management.

papers.title: Rational design and synthesis of furan-based Schiff base quinazolin-4-amine hybrids: spectral elucidation, molecular docking, DFT studies, and in silico ADMET-antioxidant study.
papers.abstract: In this work, a new series of furan-based quinazoline-4-amine hydrazone (Schiff base) derivatives (4a-h) was rationally designed and synthesized in good yields (84-90%) through a multistep route involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, and hydrazone/Schiff base condensation reactions. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and ESI-mass spectrometry, which confirmed the proposed structures. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to optimize the molecular geometries and to derive frontier molecular orbital
papers.summary: This paper reports the rational design and synthesis of eight new furan-based quinazolin-4-amine Schiff base hybrids (4a-h) using a multistep route combining nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, and hydrazone condensation, with structures confirmed by FT-IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. DFT calculations were used to optimize geometries and analyze frontier molecular orbitals, and the compounds were evaluated in silico via molecular docking and ADMET-antioxidant predictions. The work is a medicinal chemistry synthesis and computational modeling study rather than a biological validation study.

papers.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge.
papers.abstract: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent perform
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid machine learning framework for predicting blood-brain barrier permeability by combining transformer-derived molecular embeddings with traditional physicochemical descriptors using late-stage ensemble fusion. Trained on B3DB and NeuTox datasets and evaluated on the BBBP benchmark, the approach aims to overcome the limitations of descriptor-only methods (lack of structural context) and pure deep learning methods (overfitting). The model showed strong, dataset-dependent predictive performance.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction into a single workflow, using LLM-driven agents to coordinate specialized network-based algorithms. It aims to overcome the fragmentation of existing tools by letting users interact in natural language while the system orchestrates heterogeneous data and analyses. The platform is presented as a development study, with the abstract emphasizing the design rationale rather than quantitative validation.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the structure of the antifungal protein NFAP2, which binds fungus-specific intracellular targets like glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, to guide structure-based drug repurposing against Candida albicans. By leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles, the authors identify candidate drugs that mimic NFAP2's targeting strategy, offering a faster route to new antifungal therapies amid rising resistance and limited treatment options.

papers.title: Graphics processing unit-accelerated quantum simulation for molecular biology and drug discovery: algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has intensified the need for methods that describe molecular systems with quantum-mechanical accuracy. Gate-based quantum computing offers a principled framework for simulating electronic structure, molecular interactions, and biological processes at a fidelity inaccessible to classical force fields or density functional theory alone, yet scarce, noisy hardware limits direct experimentation. Graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated quantum simulation has emerged as a practical bridge, allowing quantum algorithms to be developed, validated, and benchmarked on classical
papers.summary: This review surveys how GPUs can accelerate classical simulation of quantum algorithms for molecular biology and drug discovery, covering algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications. It argues that GPU-accelerated quantum simulation serves as a practical bridge for developing and benchmarking quantum algorithms despite scarce, noisy quantum hardware.

papers.title: Machine learning for RNA-small molecule interactions: methodologies, evaluation, and future directions.
papers.abstract: RNA is emerging as a compelling therapeutic target due to its rich structural diversity and central involvement in gene regulation, splicing, translation, and cellular signaling. Alongside advances in structural biology, computational approaches, especially machine learning and deep learning, have transformed the systematic analysis of RNA-small molecule interactions. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of computational methods for RNA-small molecule interaction prediction, with a particular emphasis on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning and deep learning methods for predicting RNA-small molecule interactions, focusing on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and related interaction modeling. It organizes the computational landscape, discusses evaluation practices, and outlines future directions for RNA-targeted drug discovery. The paper serves as a structured reference for researchers applying ML to RNA as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit.
papers.abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical p
papers.summary: This tutorial presents a reproducible Jupyter notebook workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling of 200 CDK2 inhibitors from ChEMBL, combining RDKit preprocessing with the graph neural network platform ADMET-AI 2.0. It demonstrates how to compute physicochemical properties and predict pharmacokinetic and toxicity endpoints in a practical, step-by-step manner. The contribution is primarily educational, showing how existing tools can be integrated into a standard cheminformatics pipeline.

papers.title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.
papers.summary: This news and perspectives article reports on recent efforts to use AI models to identify existing drugs that could be repurposed to treat antibiotic-resistant infections. It highlights how machine learning can accelerate and reduce the cost of drug discovery in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Utilising digital technologies for mycetoma management: A comprehensive review of advances and opportunities.
papers.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected tropical disease characterised by chronic, destructive infections of subcutaneous tissues, predominantly affecting populations in endemic regions with limited healthcare resources. Delayed diagnosis, limited treatment options, and restricted access to specialised healthcare contribute to substantial morbidity, disability, and socioeconomic burden. Digital technologies offer promising opportunities to address these challenges and improve mycetoma care. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support early detection and diagnostic accuracy through the analysis of clinical images
papers.summary: This review examines how digital technologies—particularly AI-based image analysis—could improve the diagnosis and management of mycetoma, a neglected tropical disease causing chronic subcutaneous infections in resource-limited regions. The authors highlight opportunities for earlier detection and better care access, while noting persistent barriers such as limited healthcare infrastructure and diagnostic capacity.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Novel Inhibitors of Escherichia coli MurB.
papers.abstract: MurB, a key enzyme involved in bacterial cell wall biosynthesis, represents a promising target for antibacterial drug discovery. In this study, a machine learning assay was employed to identify potential inhibitors targeting E. coli MurB. Five machine learning models were constructed using AutoMolDesigner, of which the RDKit_2D-based Model_2 was selected as the optimal activity-prediction model for virtual screening of an in-house compound library, yielding 238 compounds. These compounds were subsequently subjected to FRED molecular docking, and 16 candidate compounds were selected based on th
papers.summary: The authors built five machine-learning models to predict MurB inhibition and used the best-performing RDKit 2D model to virtually screen an in-house compound library, yielding 238 hits that were then narrowed by FRED molecular docking to 16 candidates. This demonstrates a combined ML-plus-docking workflow for antibacterial lead discovery against a validated cell-wall biosynthesis target. The work is a straightforward application of existing tools to a specific target rather than a methodological advance.

papers.title: Crystallographic fragment screening in cancer and antiviral drug discovery: from electron density to translational outcomes.
papers.abstract: Crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) provides an experimental starting point for small-molecule discovery by defining a fragment's binding site, pose and routes for chemical elaboration. By establishing a structural hypothesis before major medicinal-chemistry investment, CFS reduces early uncertainty and the risk of pursuing a binding mode inferred from activity or modeling but not supported by experimental structural evidence.
papers.summary: This review discusses crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) as an experimental approach for early-stage drug discovery, particularly in cancer and antiviral applications. CFS identifies where and how small fragment molecules bind to target proteins, providing a structural basis for guiding chemical optimization before major medicinal-chemistry investment. The authors argue this reduces uncertainty and risk compared to binding modes inferred from activity data or modeling alone.

papers.title: A multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform with composite and domain-level validity for identification of mild cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a clinically heterogeneous syndrome that can represent an early manifestation of neurodegenerative disease. Diagnosis relies on assessments that are difficult to scale, leaving many individuals unidentified.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study presents a multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform that combines multiple digital assessments to identify mild cognitive impairment, with validity demonstrated at both composite and domain levels. The approach aims to provide a scalable alternative to conventional MCI diagnostics, which are difficult to administer at population scale and leave many cases undetected.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
papers.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribos
papers.summary: This review integrates the chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and genomic regulation of antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi. It highlights that most biosynthetic gene clusters in these fungi are silent under standard lab conditions, and surveys strategies for activating cryptic BGCs to unlock unexplored chemical diversity. The work connects metabolite discovery with genomics and biotechnology approaches for antibacterial drug development.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor-target interactions. Their approach argues that geometric alignment of pretrained embeddings can outperform complex deep architectures, particularly when training data is scarce and generalization to new chemical scaffolds is needed.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
papers.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly lo
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI methods—object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents—are transforming animal behavioral phenotyping for preclinical pharmacology and therapeutic discovery. It argues that these tools overcome the labor-intensity, low dimensionality, and poor reproducibility of conventional behavioral scoring by extracting richer spatial, temporal, and phenotypic information from video.

papers.title: From phenotypic screening to target and compound prioritization for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is a progressive kidney disorder with limited therapeutic options, highlighting an urgent need for safer, long-term treatments. This study presents a multi-step computational and experimental approach to identify and assess target-based hypotheses for mechanisms underlying the cAMP-dependent cyst swelling. We analyzed phenotypic screening data from a 3D mIMCD3-Pkd1-/- forskolin-induced, cAMP-driven cyst swelling (CS) assay, classifying compounds based on their CS activity. These compounds were cross-referenced with the Papyrus database to id
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study describes a multi-step computational and experimental pipeline that starts from phenotypic screening data in a 3D ADPKD cyst-swelling assay and uses compound cross-referencing with the Papyrus bioactivity database to generate and prioritize target-based hypotheses for cAMP-dependent cyst swelling. The work aims to bridge phenotypic hits to actionable targets and compounds for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, where long-term therapeutic options remain limited.

papers.title: Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models.
papers.abstract: Elucidating the structures of unknown small molecules remains a major challenge in chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery. While nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the gold standard for structure elucidation, interpreting spectra remains labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge to navigate the vast space of possible structures. Here, we present an AI system for rapid, automated de novo structure elucidation that combines a molecular generative model with a scientific reasoning agent. Its generative component, CHEFNMR2, is an atomic flow-matching model that predicts smal
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present an AI system that combines a generative model (CHEFNMR2) with a scientific reasoning agent to automatically determine the chemical structures of unknown small molecules from NMR spectra. This addresses the labor-intensive, expert-dependent bottleneck in structure elucidation, which is central to chemistry and drug discovery. The approach aims to make de novo structure determination faster and more accessible.

papers.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stage
papers.summary: MultiTargetDB is a new curated database of small molecules that bind multiple biological targets, designed to support polypharmacology research and multitarget drug discovery. It integrates chemical structures (including scaffolds), drug development stages, and detailed biological annotations with measurement-level provenance. The resource addresses the scarcity of well-curated multitarget ligand datasets for complex diseases.

papers.title: Computational network pharmacology and molecular simulations to explore the potential mechanisms of Pyrrosia piloselloides compounds against prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in men worldwide. Emerging evidence highlights the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides or P. piloselloides) has demonstrated anticancer potential, but its molecular mechanisms against prostate cancer remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate its potential anticancer compounds and underlying molecular mechanisms using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
papers.summary: This study uses computational network pharmacology and molecular simulation to predict which compounds from the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides) might act against prostate cancer and through which molecular targets. It is an in silico screen that generates hypotheses about mechanisms rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit
papers.summary: This review discusses how LC-MS metabolomic profiling, combined with expanding spectral databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation, is improving the characterization of complex natural product metabolomes. It highlights how AI-enabled navigation of natural product chemical space can help overcome low annotation rates and rediscovery of known metabolites, accelerating natural product-based drug discovery and biotechnology.

papers.title: Human Plasma Causal Immunome-Phenome Mapping Reveals Cardiovascular Enrichment and Therapeutic Target Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Circulating immune proteins represent an important class of therapeutic targets, but existing proteome-wide genetic studies have not systematically resolved immune-related target-disease relationships across a broad disease phenome within a unified framework that integrates causal inference, locus colocalization, orthogonal protein-level support, independent replication, and standardized evidence grading.
papers.summary: This study maps causal relationships between circulating immune proteins and a broad range of diseases using genetic instruments, integrating causal inference, colocalization, orthogonal protein-level evidence, replication, and standardized evidence grading. The authors report enrichment of cardiovascular disease associations and identify immune-protein targets with therapeutic potential. The work provides a systematic framework for prioritizing immune-related drug targets across the human phenome.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which protein targets might explain the anticancer activity of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus species. No new compounds were isolated and no new cytotoxicity experiments were performed; the work builds entirely on prior chemical and biological data. The authors propose candidate anticancer targets for these natural products, offering hypotheses for future experimental validation.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used LC-HRMS/MS molecular networking (GNPS) to profile the metabolites of Scoparia dulcis aerial parts, then combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations with experimental validation to identify bioactive constituents and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The work links specific phytochemicals to putative anti-inflammatory targets and pathways, providing a mechanistic rationale for the traditional use of this edible herb.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study shows that the length of the lipid tail on carmofur analogs determines how they disrupt membranes, revealing membrane interactions beyond carmofur's known enzyme-inhibition mechanisms. The findings suggest these amphiphilic compounds can act through noncanonical, membrane-mediated modes of action, which matters for understanding both their anticancer and antiviral repurposing potential.

papers.title: Navigating the Pharma 4.0 revolution: how AI-enabled applications and predictive modelling shaped pharmaceutical development in the post-pandemic era: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Pharma 4.0 is touted to make processes more efficient and resilient to unforeseen circumstances, boosting productivity, speed and accuracy of pharmaceutical systems. Besides operational stability, these technological implementations could potentially improve clinical outcomes. AI-enabled Pharma 4.0 applications and predictive modelling are utilised in pharmaceutical development for the discovery of new compounds that could potentially be used as drugs for COVID-19. This systematic review examined how contemporary Pharma 4.0 technologies have impacted pharmaceutical development in the post COVI
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how AI-enabled Pharma 4.0 technologies and predictive modelling have influenced pharmaceutical development in the post-COVID era, with particular attention to drug discovery for COVID-19 compounds. The authors synthesize evidence on how these technologies improve process efficiency, resilience, and productivity across pharmaceutical systems, and discuss their potential to enhance clinical outcomes beyond operational stability.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
papers.abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. With strengths in multi-omics integration, complex pattern recognition, and
papers.summary: This review argues that AI can serve as an integrated toolkit across the antibacterial drug discovery pipeline, from target identification and multi-omics data integration to compound screening and resistance prediction. It frames AI applications around distinct resistance mechanisms and translational stages, addressing the gap between generic AI enthusiasm and concrete use in overcoming antimicrobial resistance. The paper emphasizes that single-mechanism drug design and slow discovery pipelines make a staged, AI-supported strategy necessary.

papers.title: Computational drug screening for drug-resistant tuberculosis: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches-including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks-have substantially expande
papers.summary: This review surveys computational approaches for discovering new drugs against drug-resistant tuberculosis, covering virtual screening, AI-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks. It highlights how these methods have expanded the search space for anti-TB agents while discussing remaining challenges and future directions. The paper is a broad overview rather than a primary research contribution.

papers.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC5A12 as a marker of an invasive epithelial state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This state is linked to immune remodeling within the tumor microenvironment and points to a potential therapeutic vulnerability. The work helps define how malignant epithelial heterogeneity relates to immune changes and treatment targets in HNSCC.

papers.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
papers.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor
papers.summary: The authors used the BindCraft protein design tool to computationally design short peptides that bind the nucleosome acidic patch, a key chromatin interaction hub. They then experimentally validated that the designed peptides bind their target, demonstrating that de novo peptide design can be applied to chromatin interfaces. This provides a starting point for engineered tools or epigenetic therapeutics targeting nucleosome surfaces.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to identify ion channel-related genes as potential biomarkers in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The authors highlight that human ion channel genes are core effectors of transmembrane signaling and may contribute to COPD initiation and progression, though the mechanisms remain unclear. The work aims to establish the potential diagnostic or mechanistic value of ion channel gene signatures in COPD.

papers.title: AI-enabled drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease: from computational nomination to pharmacological proof.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the scale and speed of drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Transcriptomic signature matching, network-based systems pharmacology, real-world data pharmacoepidemiology and multi-omics machine learning have generated hundreds of candidate drugs, while repurposed agents account for 35% (56 of 158) of drugs and 42% (15 of 36) of Phase 3 agents in the 2026 AD pipeline. Clinical translation, however, remains unproven. Randomised trials of GLP-1 receptor agonists illustrate the gap between prioritisation and therapeutic proof: semaglutide did not sl
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI methods—transcriptomic signature matching, network pharmacology, real-world pharmacoepidemiology, and multi-omics machine learning—have generated hundreds of candidate repurposing hits for Alzheimer's disease, with repurposed drugs now making up 35% of the 2026 AD pipeline and 42% of Phase 3 agents. The authors emphasize that computational nomination has outpaced clinical validation, citing the semaglutide trial as an example of the gap between AI prioritization and pharmacological proof.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of Coumarin-Triazole Derivatives Targeting the Conserved QGDNQ Motif of Chandipura RdRp.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV) is a recently discovered neurotropic virus associated with severe encephalitis in children and for which there is currently no specific antiviral treatment. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is an attractive antiviral target because of its essential role in viral RNA synthesis and the presence of conserved catalytic motifs required for polymerase function. In this study, a structure-based computational approach was employed to investigate coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors targeting the conserved QGDNQ motif-containing region of CHPV RdRp.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structure-based methods to screen coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of the Chandipura virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, targeting its conserved QGDNQ catalytic motif. The work identifies candidate compounds in silico for a virus that currently lacks any approved antiviral treatment. Experimental validation of the predicted binders is not described in the abstract.

papers.title: Targeting IL-1R1 and androgen receptor using natural compounds from Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum: an in silico and in vitro study.
papers.abstract: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and in vitro assays to identify natural compounds from two medicinal plants (Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum) that can simultaneously inhibit IL-1R1 (an inflammation receptor) and the androgen receptor, two targets implicated in lung and prostate cancer. The authors propose that dual targeting of inflammatory and hormone signaling pathways could help overcome therapeutic resistance, though the findings are preliminary and require further validation.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally docks ebelin lactone, a plant-derived triterpenoid, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including those involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. The work extends prior findings of its binding to M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors by systematically profiling its structural compatibility across a broader set of cognition-associated targets. It is a purely in silico docking analysis without experimental validation.

papers.title: Mapping the subcellular pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic landscape: a systems-pharmacology framework for predicting combination therapies against intracellular bacterial infections.
papers.abstract: Intracellular bacterial pathogens represent one of the most formidable challenges in contemporary medicine. By exploiting host cellular niches, these organisms evade immune surveillance and withstand conventional antibiotic therapies, establishing persistent reservoirs that are difficult to eradicate. Although antibiotic combinations, host-directed interventions, and drug repurposing have shown promise, conventional discovery pipelines rarely capture the dynamic and compartmentalized nature of the intracellular environment. This review proposes a systems pharmacology framework centered on subc
papers.summary: This review proposes a systems pharmacology framework that maps how drugs move through and act within subcellular compartments to predict combination therapies against intracellular bacterial infections. It argues that conventional drug discovery pipelines ignore the dynamic, compartmentalized nature of host cells where pathogens hide, and that explicitly modeling subcellular pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics could improve combination and repurposing strategies.

papers.title: Plasmid-Mediated AmpC Detection in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: In Vitro Prevalence and In Silico Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in clinical specimens collected in Lahore, Pakistan, and aimed to identify potential inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases.
papers.journal: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
papers.summary: This study screened clinical E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates from Lahore, Pakistan, for plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamases and then used computational docking to propose candidate small-molecule inhibitors against these enzymes. It combines local prevalence surveillance with early-stage in silico drug design, though the inhibitors have not yet been experimentally validated.

papers.title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
papers.abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensio
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches—network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation—to predict how the environmental pollutant 6PPD-quinone might contribute to intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways, suggesting that 6PPD-Q could activate stress-related responses (e.g., mitochondrial membrane potential and antioxidant response element) in disc tissue. The work is entirely predictive and lacks experimental validation.
